title: Qt: Replace plugin column "Path" with "Scope" in About dialog
description:
Instead of using a Path field, that is really long and contains
a lot of redundant information, use a scope field that indicates
if the plugin is a personal plugin (loaded from the personal plugins
folder) or a global plugin (loaded from the global plugins folder).

Together with the plugin name this allows to construct the path
completely. By right-clicking on the row it is possible to open the file
browser in the correct plugin path and the personal/global plugin
folder path itself is displayed elsewhere.

Extcap and Lua scripts need to be enhanced to provide this
information too.

[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/13575/diffs?diff_id=865087721&start_sha=f5280dea76513a988da64c39fe17e153719b83d4)

_Extcap and Lua scripts need to be enhanced to provide this information too._

For Lua scripts, how would that be done, something like so?

```
local info =
{
    version = "1.0",
    author = "John Doe",
    description = "My Lua Plugin",
    scope = "user"
}

set_plugin_info(info)
```

And instead of specifying "global" or "user" for the scope, I do think "global" or "personal" is a better choice because those terms match the Folder names described in _"Help -> About Wireshark -> Folders"_, namely _"**Global** Lua Plugins"_ and _"**Personal** Lua Plugins"_.  Alternatively, we could also consider using "public" or "private" instead?

> For Lua scripts, how would that be done, something like so?

Something like that. I don't think calling set_plugin_info() is necessary but I would have to look at the code to be sure.

> And instead of specifying "global" or "user" for the scope, I do think "global" or "personal" is a better choice

Ok I will use "personal" instead of "user" for consistency. Later we can replace the term "personal" everywhere if we want.

I don't like this change because it removes functionality I use.

Earlier I could easily find where a Lua script is located (yes, we have support for two personal locations, the old ".local/lib/wireshark/plugins" and the new ".config/wireshark/plugins"), and I could double-click the link to open in my editor.

Now I can "left-click" to select "Show in Finder", but this open a Finder window with the root directory instead of the directory containing the Lua plugin.

"Show in Finder" should open the correct directory. That's a bug.

I would like to remove the deprecated plugin folder too, it's been more than one release.

I don't mind adding the Path column back either.

> I don't mind adding the Path column back either.

Done in !13612.
